name: Deferegger Heilwasserwelt St. Jakob
kurzbeschreibung: The Deferegger Heilwasserwelt in St. Jakob: 600,000-year-old fossil deep healing water from a depth of 1,850 m with a modern visitor centre and graduation tower.
beschreibung:
Overview

The fascinating Deferegger Heilwasserwelt is located on the idyllic outskirts of the national park community of St. Jakob in Defereggen in the East Tyrolean Defereggental (Lienz district) at an altitude of around 1,390 metres. Built around the thermal and mineral medicinal water source in the hamlet of Innerrotte, this modern information and health centre counts among the most extraordinary natural monuments in the Hohe Tauern. At its core lies a prehistoric geological wonder: the Deferegger Heilwasser – a highly mineralised, purest deep groundwater that rested completely protected from environmental influences for more than 600,000 years at a depth of 1,850 metres beneath the high alpine massif.

Route & Requirements

The discovery of this fossil water treasure dates back to exploratory deep geological drilling in 2004. Scientific analyses revealed a sensation celebrated worldwide: the water originates from an ancient primordial ocean and boasts an exceptionally high density with more than 60 grams of dissolved minerals and trace elements per litre (especially iodine, chloride, sodium, and sulphate). Medically certified as an official healing water, it exhibits proven therapeutic benefits for dermatological conditions (such as psoriasis and neurodermatitis) as well as chronic respiratory and joint ailments. In the modern visitor centre, a multimedia exhibition illustrates the geological formation of the Alps, the rock strata of the Defereggental, and the engineering feats of the 1,850-metre-deep drilling operation. A prominent outdoor attraction is the Deferegger Freiluft-Gradierwerk (open-air graduation tower): the pure healing brine trickles down through blackthorn brushwood, creating a saline, sea-like microclimate that visitors can deeply inhale during a leisurely stroll. Kneipp wading basins, mineral spring tasting bars, and a stylish shop offering certified natural skincare products complete the facility.

Visit & Arrival

The Deferegger Heilwasserwelt is open year-round: during the summer months (May to October) from Monday to Saturday from 09:00 to 17:00; in the winter months (December to April) from Tuesday to Saturday from 13:00 to 17:00 (closed on Sundays and public holidays). Guided tours through the visitor centre take place weekly. Admission prices (2025/2026 season): entrance to the exhibition and the graduation tower adults approx. €6.00, seniors approx. €5.00, children and youths (6 to 15 years) approx. €3.00, young children free. Holders of the Osttirol Card enjoy free admission. Getting there by car: from Lienz via the Felbertauernstraße B108 to Huben, where you turn onto the Defereggentalstraße L25 and drive about 25 km into the valley to St. Jakob, following the signs to the Heilwasserwelt (free parking available at Innerrotte 58). By public transport: ÖBB train to Lienz railway station, from where VVT bus line 953 runs directly to St. Jakob in Defereggen (stop St. Jakob Innerrotte, about a four-minute walk).

Tips

The entire visitor centre, the shop, and the circular path around the open-air graduation tower are step-free and fully wheelchair-accessible. Be sure to try the original medicinal water spray on site, which provides noticeable, immediate relief to irritated skin. Combine your excursion with a scenic hike to the idyllic Obersee lake on the Staller Sattel at the Italian border.
